title: Book: The Dhandho Investor — Mohnish Pabrai (2007)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: Mohnish Pabrai draws on the Patel family's motel businesses to describe 'dhandho' investing: look for low-risk, high-uncertainty situations, summarised as 'heads I win, tails I don't lose much'. Ideas include buying existing businesses instead of inventing new ones, focusing on a few bets you understand deeply, insisting on a margin of safety, and cloning the best ideas of others. The book is easy to read and rooted in value investing. Cautions: concentrated bets can lose a lot if your judgement is wrong, the approach assumes skill and time that beginners may not have, and past examples don't guarantee future results. It is education, not a recommendation to follow his portfolio.
